html:
The Sanavirones were an Indigenous people of central Argentina, living in northern Córdoba and southern Santiago del Estero, near the Salinas Grandes and the Dulce river.

They were settled farmers who grew maize, beans and squash and lived in villages of pit houses, some protected by thorny fences. Their neighbours were the Comechingones in the hills to the west and the Lule and Diaguita to the north. The Spanish founded Córdoba in 1573 and divided the Sanavirones among settlers as forced labour. Their language died out, and only six or seven of its words are known.
sum: The Sanavirones were an Indigenous people of central Argentina, living in northern Córdoba and southern Santiago del Estero, near the Salinas Grandes and the Dulce river.
